topics.label: Lecture framing and introduction to cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s aims and introduces the hallmarks framework for understanding loss of growth control.

topics.label: Mutations in growth and survival signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how disrupted differentiation changes cancer cell maturity and tissue organization.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered regulation of p53 and mitochondrial apoptotic factors allows cancer cells to evade programmed death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and replicative immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits normal cell replication and how increased TERT expression allows tumors to bypass that limit.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics draw together the cellular safeguards whose disruption enables cancer cells to escape normal growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how altered metabolism supports cancer and interacts with the molecular changes driving it.

topics.label: Angiogenesis and vascular support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit blood vessels to sustain growth beyond the limits of oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what enables cancer cells to spread from a primary tumor and establish detectable tumors at distant sites.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture’s learning goals, summarizes the convergence of diverse cancer routes on shared hallmarks, and offers further reading and final remarks.
